# Before NLP and Text Analysis

[One needs to know how to mine, warngle, and manipulate text data.]{.fragment fragment-index='1'}
<br><br>
[tidy priciples can make this task easy (relatively)]{.fragment fragment-index='2'}
<br><br>
[*"Treating text as data frames of individual words allows us to manipulate, summarize, and visualize the characteristics of text easily and integrate natural language processing into effective workflows..."*]{.fragment fragment-index='3'}
<br><br>
[We do this using the {tidytext} along with other know methods]{.fragment fragment-index='4'}

# Tidy Data

As described in [Wickham 2014](https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v059i10)

1. Each variable is a column.
2. Each observation is a row.
3. Each type of observational unit is a table.

# Tidy Text

As described by [Silge and Robinson 2017](https://www.tidytextmining.com/)

1. **A table with one-token-per-row**
2. token: A meaningful unit of text. (word,sentence,etc)
3. There are other forms of text data structures: string, corpus, document-term matric. (more on this later)

# Tokens

>"*A token is a meaningful unit of text, most often a word, that we are interested in using for further analysis, and tokenization is the process of splitting text into tokens.*"

# Unnesting Tokens

We need to get the text in *one-token-per-row* to acheive the Tidy Text format. This can be dome by the `unnest_tokens()` function from {tidytext}
<br>

```{r}
#| echo: true

text <- c("Because I could not stop for Death -",
          "He kindly stopped for me -",
          "The Carriage held but just Ourselves -",
          "and Immortality")

text

```

# Unnesting Tokens

Notice any punctuations?
<br>

```{r}
tibble(
  row = c(1:length(text)),
  text = text
) |>
  unnest_tokens(token = "words",output = word, input =  text)
```

# Unnesting Tokens

[Tokens can be sentences, characters, lines, paragraphs, or a regex pattern]{.fragment fragment-index='1'}
<br><br>
[Not all words are useful. We can remove *stop words*]{.fragment fragment-index='2'}


# The RBI MPC minutes

See a sample [here](https://website.rbi.org.in/documents/87730/39710918/PR1769MPCf562eb05339b404f8dc23d07725ef354.pdf)
<br>

```{r}
#| echo: false

mpc_minutes |>
  head(100) |>
  kableExtra::kable() |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling() |>
  kableExtra::scroll_box(width = '100%', height = '500px')

```


# The RBI MPC minutes

**Unnest tokens to get tidytext format**
<br>

```{r}
#| echo: true

mpc_minutes |>
  mutate(
    identifier = str_remove(identifier,".{1,}ting|.{1,}ting,")
  ) |>
  unnest_tokens(output = word,input = lines)  -> mpc_minutes_unnested

mpc_minutes_unnested
```

# The RBI MPC minutes - removing stop words

**You can choose which stop words to remove**
<br>

```{r}
#| echo: true

mpc_minutes_unnested |>
  anti_join(stop_words |>
  filter(!word %in% c("yes","no"))) -> mpc_minutes_unnested

```

# The RBI MPC Minutes - Word freq

**Notice any problems?**
<br>

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| 
mpc_minutes_unnested |>
  count(word, sort = T)

```

# Can do other stuff

**Is the MPC always attended by all the members**
<br>

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: slide

mpc_minutes |>
  group_by(identifier) |>
  summarise(
    attend_all = ifelse(sum(str_detect(lines,"was attended by all the members")) ==1,"Yes","No")
  ) |>
    ggplot(aes(x=""))+
    geom_bar(aes(fill = attend_all),
    position = "fill",
    width = 0.25)+
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("#b35a54ff","#6c8562ff"))+
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      aspect.ratio = 0.25
    )+
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0)),limits = c(0,1))+
    scale_x_discrete(expand =  expansion(mult = c(0, 0)))+
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL,
      title = "Proportion of MPC meetings that do not have all members present.",
      subtitle = "Green rpresents meetings with all members present. Red represents one or more absent members. n=58"
    ) +
    coord_flip()

```

# Can do other stuff

**Is the decision making in the MPC usually unanimous?** [doc](https://website.rbi.org.in/documents/d/rbi/pr570202526_rbi) [doc1](https://website.rbi.org.in/documents/87730/39710918/PR1769MPCf562eb05339b404f8dc23d07725ef354.pdf)
<br>

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: slide

mpc_minutes |>
  filter(str_detect(lines, "[:alpha:]{1,}\\s{1,}Yes$") | str_detect(lines, "[:alpha:]{1,}\\s{1,}No$") | 
  str_detect(lines, "[:alpha:]{1,}\\s{1,}Yes\\s{1,}[:digit:]{2}$") | str_detect(lines, "[:alpha:]{1,}\\s{1,}No\\s{1,}[:digit:]{2}$")) |>
  mutate(
    identifier = str_remove(identifier,"Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting"),
    identifier = paste0(str_extract(identifier,"[:alpha:]{1,} "),str_extract(identifier," [:digit:]{4}")),
    individual = str_squish(str_extract(lines,"^.{1,}(?=Yes|No)")),
    identifier = lubridate::my(identifier),
    decision = str_squish(str_extract(lines," Yes| No| Yes | No "))
  ) |> 
  select(-lines) |>
  ggplot(aes(identifier)) +
  geom_bar(aes(fill = decision)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#b35a54ff","#6c8562ff"))+
    labs(
      title = "MPC decisions across time.",
      x = NULL,
      y = "Number of Members",
      subtitle = "Green represents members in favour of resolution. Red represents members not in favour. n=58. 19/58 are not unanimous."
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0)),limits = c(0,6))+
    scale_x_date(expand =  expansion(mult = c(0, 0)),
    breaks = scales::breaks_width("2 months"),
    labels = scales::label_date("%m-%y")
     )+
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      legend.position = "none"
    ) 


```

# Can do other stuff

**who say no?**
<br>

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: slide
mpc_minutes |>
  filter(str_detect(lines, "[:alpha:]{1,}\\s{1,}Yes$") | str_detect(lines, "[:alpha:]{1,}\\s{1,}No$") | 
  str_detect(lines, "[:alpha:]{1,}\\s{1,}Yes\\s{1,}[:digit:]{2}$") | str_detect(lines, "[:alpha:]{1,}\\s{1,}No\\s{1,}[:digit:]{2}$")) |>
  mutate(
    identifier = str_remove(identifier,"Minutes of the Monetary Policy Committee Meeting"),
    identifier = paste0(str_extract(identifier,"[:alpha:]{1,} "),str_extract(identifier," [:digit:]{4}")),
    individual = str_squish(str_extract(lines,"^.{1,}(?=Yes|No)")),
    identifier = lubridate::my(identifier),
    decision = str_squish(str_extract(lines," Yes| No| Yes | No "))
  ) |> 
  select(-lines) |>
  mutate(
    individual = ifelse(str_detect(individual,"Dr.[:alpha:]"),
    str_replace(individual,pattern = "Dr.","Dr. "),
    individual)
    ) |>
  group_by(individual) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    in_favour = sum(decision == "Yes"),
    not_in_favour = n - in_favour
  ) |>
    arrange(desc(n)) |>
    kableExtra::kable() |>
    kableExtra::kable_styling() |>
    kableExtra::scroll_box(width = '100%', height = '500px')
```

# All this is fine. Where is the cool stuff?

# Sentiment Analysis

[With word frequencies we can compare what is relatively more or less important across a selection of documents. (With some caution)]{.fragment fragment-index='1'}
<br><br>
[But it would be better to get an understanding of the *opinion* or *sentiment* behid the text.]{.fragment fragment-index='2'}
<br><br>
[What is the text trying to convey? Doom, Acche din (good times), Caution, negativity, etc.]{.fragment fragment-index='3'}
<br><br>
[Text mining can help us to programmatically find the emotional content of a text.]{.fragment fragment-index='4'}

# Sentiment Analysis

> We will consider the sentiment of an entire text as the sum of sentiment content of thee individual words of the text.

<br>
*This is one of the approaches*

# Sentiment Analysis - Lexicons

[For the tidytext format, unigram based lexicons are suited.]{.fragment fragment-index='1'}
<br>
[Three general purpose lexicons are `AFINN`, `bing`, and `nrc`.]{.fragment fragment-index='2'}
<br>
[These are available through the {tidytext}.]{.fragment fragment-index='3'}
<br>
[These do not contain all possible english words. Many words are neutral.]{.fragment fragment-index='4'}
<br>
[Developed through croudsourcing or by authors, are validate by some combination of approaches.]{.fragment fragment-index='5'}
<br>
[What care should be taken while choosing a lexicon?]{.fragment fragment-index='6'}

# Sentiment Analysis - AFINN

**Words are assigned a score between [-5,5]. Negative scores indicate negative sentiments and positve scores indicate positive sentiments**

<br>

```{r}
get_sentiments("afinn")
```

# Sentiment Analysis - bing

**Classifies words in to a binary: positive or negative**

<br>

```{r}
get_sentiments("bing")
```

# Sentiment Analysis - nrc

**"categorizes words in a binary fashion (“yes”/“no”) into categories of positive, negative, anger, anticipation, disgust, fear, joy, sadness, surprise, and trust"**

<br>

```{r}
get_sentiments("nrc")
```

## Sentiment Analysis - Use with Care

**Unigram based approaches have issues with qualifier words**

> There is a decline in growth.

> This is not good.

## Subjectivity in Sentiment Analysis

**Ref: [Sentiment Analysis and Subjectivity ](https://www.cs.uic.edu/~liub/FBS/NLP-handbook-sentiment-analysis.pdf)**

> *“(1) I bought an iPhone a few days ago. (2) It was such a nice phone. (3) The touch screen was
really cool. (4) The voice quality was clear too. (5) Although the battery life was not long, that is
ok for me. (6) However, my mother was mad with me as I did not tell her before I bought it. (7)
She also thought the phone was too expensive, and wanted me to return it to the shop. … ”*

**Who/What are these opinions about? Who is making/providing these opinions?**

# Looking for Sentiments in the RBI MPC Minutes

Once again, lets look at the [doc](https://website.rbi.org.in/documents/87730/39710918/PR1769MPCf562eb05339b404f8dc23d07725ef354.pdf).

# Looking for Sentiments in the RBI MPC Minutes

> The real stuff is in para 6 and later. (Assessments, Outlook, Rationale, and Statements)

# MPC Sentiments - Set up

**While we use words as unit of analyses, we aggregate at Para level**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: slide

  mpc_minutes |> 
  # Mark Para number for each line from the MPC
  filter(str_length(str_squish(lines))>2)|> 
  mutate(
    lines = str_squish(lines),
    para_num = str_extract(lines,pattern = "^[:digit:]{1,2}\\. ")
  ) |> 
  fill(para_num , .direction = "down") |>
  mutate(
    para_num = str_remove_all(para_num, "[:punct:]") |> str_squish() |> as.integer()
  ) |> 
  # Keep only relevant para of the MPC
  filter(para_num >= 6) |>
  # Get in one-word-per-row shape
  unnest_tokens(word, lines) -> mpc_sentiments_setup

  mpc_sentiments_setup


```

# MPC Sentiments - augment with lexicon

```{r}
#| echo: true

mpc_sentiments_setup |>
  # rermove stop words |>
  anti_join(stop_words) |> 
  # join with sentiments lexicon
  inner_join(get_sentiments("bing")) -> mpc_sentiments_augmented

  mpc_sentiments_augmented

```

# MPC Sentiments - Aggregate at Para level

```{r}
#| echo: true

 mpc_sentiments_augmented |>
  # get MPC para level sentiment
  group_by(identifier, para_num) |>
    summarise(
      pos = sum(sentiment == "positive")/n(),
      neg = sum(sentiment == "negative")/n(),
      tot = pos + neg
    ) |>
  ungroup() -> mpc_sentiments_bing

mpc_sentiments_bing
```

# MPC Sentiments - Bing

```{r}
#| echo: true

mpc_sentiments_bing |>
   # Get the MPC identifier as date
  mutate(
    identifier = str_remove(identifier,".{1,} Meeting|.{1,} Meeting,"),
    identifier = str_remove(identifier,"^,"),
    identifier = str_remove(identifier,"[.{1,}]"),
    mpc_date = lubridate::my(paste0(str_extract(str_squish(identifier),"^[:alpha:]{1,}"), str_extract(identifier," [:digit:]{4}")))
  ) |>
  select(mpc_date, para_num, pos, neg, tot) -> mpc_sentiments_bing

mpc_sentiments_bing

```

# Sentence as Token

**Using {Sentimentr}** see [highlight file](rbi-mpc-for-text-analyses/mpc-highlight.html).

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true

mpc_minutes |>
  # Mark Para number for each line from the MPC
  filter(str_length(str_squish(lines))>2)|> 
  mutate(
    lines = str_squish(lines),
    para_num = str_extract(lines,pattern = "^[:digit:]{1,2}\\. ")
  ) |> 
  fill(para_num , .direction = "down") |>
  mutate(
    para_num = str_remove_all(para_num, "[:punct:]") |> str_squish() |> as.integer()
  ) |> 
  # Keep only relevant para of the MPC
  filter(para_num >= 6) |>
  # Clean identifier
   mutate(
    identifier = str_remove(identifier,".{1,} Meeting|.{1,} Meeting,"),
    identifier = str_remove(identifier,"^,"),
    identifier = str_remove(identifier,"[.{1,}]"),
    identifier = lubridate::my(paste0(str_extract(str_squish(identifier),"^[:alpha:]{1,}"), str_extract(identifier," [:digit:]{4}")))
  ) |>
  group_by(identifier,para_num) |>
  summarise(
    text = str_c(lines,collapse = " ")
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    split_para = get_sentences(text)
  ) %$%
  sentiment_by(split_para, list(identifier,para_num), polartity_dt = lexicon::hash_sentiment_loughran_mcdonald) -> snetence_para_sentiment_mpc

snetence_para_sentiment_mpc

```

## Sentence as token


```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 8

snetence_para_sentiment_mpc |>
  ggplot(aes(para_num,as.character(identifier))) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = ave_sentiment),colour = "#ffffff") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(high = "#4575b4",low = "#d73027",mid = "#ffffbf")+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(6,125,2),expand = expansion(mult = c(0,0)))+
  guides(fill = guide_colourbar(barwidth = 15))+
  labs(
    y = NULL,
    x = "Paragrapha Number",
    title = "Average sentiment in a Para using LM lexicon"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank() 
  )
```

# Beyond Descriptive

> We have seen ways to perfrom some form of descriptive analysis on text data. Some of this can be extended in building features for modeling exercises.

# Topic Modeling
<br>

> We might need to divide documents in different groups to better understand what are these about.

<br>

*We use Topic Modeling, a unsupervised classification methods, to "cluseter" documents in different natural groups*

# Topic Modeling

[Latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) used for topic modeling]{.fragment fragment-index='1'}
<br><br>
[Each doc is treated(modeled) as a (finite)mixture of topics]{.fragment fragment-index='2'}
<br><br>
[Each tpoic is treated as a mixture of words]{.fragment fragment-index='3'}
<br><br>
[Allows for overlap, complete discrete groups are not necessary]{.fragment fragment-index='4'}

# LDA

[See paper](https://jmlr.org/papers/volume3/blei03a/blei03a.pdf) for theory/Math.

[**Doc as mixture of topics**: MPC1 can be about fuel inflation due to stressed middle east conditions. This can be 10% of MPC1. MPC14 can be about food grain inflation due to poor rain. This can be 20% of MPC14...]{.fragment fragment-index='1'}
<br><br>

[**Topic as mixture of words**: Let us say that MPCs can be about topics like agri production, fuel price shocks, fiscal space. Each of these topics can be realted to different words. Words can overlap across topics.]{.fragment fragment-index='2'}

# LDA

Simultaneously, LDA estimates:

1. mixture of words associated with each topic 
2. mixture of topics associate with each document

# Applying LDA

A collection of speeches given by Dr Manmohan Singh is available [here](https://archive.org/details/selectedspeeches03unse).
<br><br>
These are speeches delivered in year 2006-07. On various topics at various occasions/locations.
<br><br>
My goal is to demonstrate how to apply LDA on these text to group them in a given number of topics. 
<br><br>
Lets see what comes out.

# Applying LDA

**The data**
<br>

```{r}
#| echo: true

speech_data
```


# Applying LDA

**Convert data to tidytext format**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: slide
speech_data|>
  unnest_tokens(word,text) -> speech_data_tidy

speech_data_tidy

```

# Applying LDA

**get word counts by doc**


```{r}
#| echo: true

speech_data_tidy |>
  anti_join(stop_words)|>
  count(title,word,sort = T) -> words_count_speech_data

words_count_speech_data
```

# Applying LDA

**Convert tidy data to dopcument term Matrix**<br>
Each row is a doc, each column is a term, values are freq of appearance
<br>

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: slide

words_count_speech_data |>
  cast_dtm(title,word,n) -> speech_dtm

speech_dtm
```

# Applying LDA

**I believe MPC minutes can have around 4 topics**

```{r}
#| echo: true

speech_lda <- LDA(speech_dtm,k = 4)

```

# Infering from LDA

**How are the topics and speeches grouped?**
<br>

```{r}
#| echo: true

tibble(
  title = speech_lda |> get_topics() |> names(),
  topic = speech_lda |> get_topics()
 ) |>
  arrange(topic)

```


# Infering from LDA

**Per-topic-per-word probablities**
<br>

```{r}
#| echo: true

tidy(speech_lda, matric = "beta") -> speech_beta

speech_beta
```

# Infering from LDA

**Per-topic-per-word probablities**
<br>

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: slide

speech_beta |>
  group_by(topic) |>
  slice_max(beta, n=10) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(topic,-beta)|>
  mutate(
    term = reorder_within(term,beta,topic)
  ) |>
    ggplot(aes(beta,term)) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = factor(topic))) +
    facet_wrap(~topic, scales = "free") +
    scale_y_reordered() +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
```

# Infering from LDA

**You can also show term probablities as distance across two topics**
<br>
The distance between the probability of a term `k` in topic `A` and topic `B`, for all `K` terms.
<br><br>
in our case this can be done for `K` terms across pairs of topics `1-2`,`1-3`,`1-4`,`2-3`,`2-4`,`3-4`
<br><br>
Since some probablities are very small, best show the distance as $log_2(\frac{\beta_2}{\beta_1})$

# Inferring from LDA

**per-document-per-topic probabilities**
<br>

```{r}
#| echo: true

speech_lda |>
  tidy(matrix = "gamma") |>
  arrange(document)
```

# Finding the right `k`

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| cache: true
#| output-location: slide
FindTopicsNumber(
  speech_dtm,
  topics = c(2:60),
  metrics = c("Griffiths2004", "CaoJuan2009", "Arun2010", "Deveaud2014"),
  method = "Gibbs",
  mc.cores = 3L,
  verbose = TRUE) -> results_lda_speech
```

# Finding the right `k`

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: slide

FindTopicsNumber_plot(results_lda_speech)
```

# Supervised models for text analysis

> Deep learning examples

# Dense Neural Netowrks

**Densely-connected neural network (feed-forward)**

![from smltar](https://smltar.com/diagram-files/dnn-architecture.png)


# Dense Neural Network

[Input is provided all at once]{.fragment fragment-index='1'}
<br><br>
[Inputs are fully connected to the first hidden layer (densely)]{.fragment fragment-index='2'}
<br><br>
["Neurons" of a given layer are only connected to the next layer]{.fragment fragment-index='3'}
<br><br>
[The number of layers and the number of neurons in a layer are variable and are  hyperparameter of the model]{.fragment fragment-index='4'}
<br><br>
[What is not accurate in the previous image?]{.fragment fragment-index='5'}

# Dense Neural Network

> Our goal is to build a binary classification model.

We use data from Reuters on news description. We try to classify news based on description.

# Dense Neural Network

**Data**

```{r}
#| echo: false

read_csv("C:/Users/ayush/Downloads/train.csv") -> news

news |>
  janitor::clean_names()|>
  mutate(
    class_index = as.factor(class_index),
    combined_text = paste(title,description,sep = ". ")
  ) -> news

  glimpse(news |> select(class_index,combined_text))
```


# Dense Neural Network

**Traing and Test sets**
<br>

```{r}
#| echo: true

news |>
  rsample::initial_split() -> news_split

news_train <- rsample::training(news_split)

news_test <- rsample::testing(news_split)
```


# Dense Neural Network

**Pre-processing**
<br>
[Sequences are modeled. Need to choose a max length of sequence.]{.fragment fragment-index='1'}
<br><br>
[Observations(docs/articles/chapters) longer than the chosen sequence are truncated]{.fragment fragment-index='2'}
<br><br>
[Observations shorter than the chosen sequence are cushioned by non-informative value]{.fragment fragment-index='3'}
<br><br>
[Sequence lenght is a hyperparamenter.]{.fragment fragment-index='4'}
<br><br>
[Best sequence lenght is something that does not waste too much information and doesnt add too many non-informative values]{.fragment fragment-index='5'}

# Dense Neural Networks

**Pre-processing**
<br>

```{r}
#| echo: false

news_train |>
  mutate(
    n_words = tokenizers::count_words(combined_text)
  ) |>
    ggplot(aes(n_words)) +
     geom_bar() + 
     theme_minimal()

```

# Dense Neural Networks

**Pre-processing**
<br>

```{r}
#| echo: true

max_words <- 3e4

max_length <- 80

```

# Dense Neural Networks

**Feature Engineeing**
<br>

```{r}
#| echo: true

news_recipe <- recipe(
  ~ combined_text,
  data = news_train
  ) |>
    step_tokenize(combined_text) |>
    step_tokenfilter(combined_text, max_tokens = max_words) |>
    step_sequence_onehot(combined_text, sequence_length = max_length,
    truncating = "post")

```

# Dense Neural Networks

**Feature Engineeing**
<br>

1. one-hot sequence embedding transforms tokens to a numeric class so that we can perform modelling.

2. Also, one-hot sequence embedding considers the order of the tokens as well, unlike tf and tf-idf

# Dense Neural Network

**Tiny example of what features* look like**

```{r}
#| echo: true

small_data <- tibble(
  text = c("Adventure Dice Game",
           "Spooky Dice Game",
           "Illustrated Book of Monsters",
           "Monsters, Ghosts, Goblins, Me, Myself and I")
)

small_spec <- recipe(~ text, data = small_data) %>%
  step_tokenize(text) %>%
  step_sequence_onehot(text, sequence_length = 6, prefix = "")

prep(small_spec)
```

# Dense Neural Network

**Tiny example of what features* look like**

```{r}
#| echo: true

prep(small_spec) %>%
  tidy(2)

```

# Dense Neural Network

**Tiny example of what features* look like** (where are the monsters in the matrix ?)

```{r}
#| echo: true

prep(small_spec) %>%
  bake(new_data = NULL, composition = "matrix")

```

# Dense Neural Network

```{r}
#| echo: true

news_prep <- prep(news_recipe)

news_train_prepped <- bake(news_prep,
      new_data = NULL, 
      composition = "matrix")

dim(news_train_prepped)

```

# Dense Neural Network

**A simple flattened dense network**

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: slide

dense_news <- keras_model_sequential(input_shape = c(80)) |> # a linear stack of layers
  layer_embedding(
    input_dim = max_words + 1,
    output_dim = 12,
    input_length = max_length
  ) |>
    layer_flatten() |>
    layer_dense(units = 32, activation = "relu") |>
    layer_dense(unit = 4, activation = "softmax")

  dense_news
```

# Dense Neural Network

**A simple flattened dense network**

[`keras_model_sequential()`: compose a stack of layers with no feedback, skips or loops, i.e. **linear stack of layers**]{.fragment fragment-index='1'}
<br>

[`layer_embedding()`: Data is converted to a tensor of $n_{obs} * S_{max} * OutDim$,  in our case (90,000 * 80* 12)]{.fragment fragment-index='2'}
<br>

[`layer_flatten()`: the 12 * 80 matrix is converted into a vector with 960 features. So each news description is 960 numbers.]{.fragment fragment-index='3'}

# Dense Neural Network

**Optimization alogrithm and loss function**

```{r}
#| echo: true

dense_news |>
  compile(
    optimizer = optimizer_adam(), #"adam"
    loss = loss_sparse_categorical_crossentropy(), #"sparse_categorical_crossentropy"
    metrics = metric_sparse_categorical_accuracy() #c("accuracy")
  )

```

# Dense Neural Network

**Fitting the model**


```{r}
#| echo: true

dense_fit_news <- dense_news |>
  fit(
    x = news_train_prepped,
    y = as.integer(news_train$class_index)-1, # carefull
    batch_size = 250,
    epochs = 20,
    validation_split = 0.25
  )

dense_fit_news
```

# Dense Neural Network


```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: slide

plot(dense_fit_news) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Dense Neural Network

**Evaluate on test**
<br>

```{r}
#| echo: true

news_baked <- bake(news_prep, new_data = news_test, composition = "matrix")

dim(news_baked)
```

# Dense Neural Network


```{r}
#| echo: true

news_baked_response <- as.integer(news_test$class_index)-1

dense_fit_test <- dense_news |>
  fit(
    x = news_train_prepped,
    y = as.integer(news_train$class_index)-1, # carefull
    batch_size = 250,
    epochs = 3,
    validation_data = list(news_baked, news_baked_response)
  )

dense_fit_test
```

# Dense Neural Network


```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: slide

plot(dense_fit_test) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Dense Neural Network


```{r}
#| echo: true

dense_news |> 
  evaluate(news_baked, news_baked_response)

```

# Dense Neural Network


```{r}
#| echo: true

dense_news |> 
  predict(news_baked)
```
